dockerguide.firmwareFailed.powerOnKey: If that option is not there, restart the PC yourself and press the BIOS key as soon as it powers on: often F2 or Del, F10 or Esc on HP, F1 on some Lenovo PCs.
dockerguide.title: Set up Docker on this PC
dockerguide.intro: CashPilot checks each thing Docker needs. It changes nothing by itself: every action waits for your click.
dockerguide.refreshFailed: CashPilot could not refresh the Docker checklist. Click Check again to retry.
dockersteps.elevatedPrompt: Windows shows a permission prompt. It names Windows PowerShell, because CashPilot makes this change through Windows PowerShell. If your account is not an administrator, an administrator types their password there.
dockersteps.restartAfter: Windows needs a restart to finish. CashPilot asks you first: nothing restarts until you click Restart now.
dockersteps.wslInstall.title: Turn on WSL?
dockersteps.wslInstall.heading: Turn on WSL
dockersteps.wslInstall.changes: Windows turns on WSL, its built-in Linux layer, and the Virtual Machine Platform feature WSL needs. CashPilot runs {command}, so no Linux distribution such as Ubuntu is installed: Docker brings its own.
dockersteps.wslInstall.undo: To undo, open Settings, System, Optional features, More Windows features, turn off Windows Subsystem for Linux and Virtual Machine Platform, then restart.
dockersteps.wslUpdate.title: Update WSL?
dockersteps.wslUpdate.heading: Update WSL
dockersteps.wslUpdate.changes: Windows updates WSL to its newest version with {command}. Your Linux distributions and their files stay as they are.
dockersteps.wslUpdate.after: Usually no restart is needed. If Windows asks for one, CashPilot asks you first. If Docker Desktop is open, close and reopen it afterwards.
dockersteps.wslUpdate.undo: CashPilot cannot roll WSL back. Older versions are on Microsoft's WSL releases page on GitHub.
dockersteps.dockerInstall.title: Install Docker Desktop?
dockersteps.dockerInstall.heading: Install Docker Desktop
dockersteps.dockerInstall.changes: A window opens where winget, Windows' app installer, downloads Docker Desktop from Docker and starts its installer. You answer winget's questions in that window. CashPilot never accepts Docker's terms for you: you read and accept them in Docker Desktop when it first opens.
dockersteps.dockerInstall.prompt: The Docker Desktop installer asks Windows for permission itself, so that prompt names Docker Desktop Installer, not CashPilot. If this PC has no winget, CashPilot opens Docker's download page instead.
dockersteps.dockerInstall.after: The installer may ask you to restart or sign out. CashPilot does not restart anything itself.
dockersteps.dockerInstall.undo: To undo, open Settings, Apps, Installed apps, find Docker Desktop and click Uninstall.
dockersteps.dockerInstall.choices: When Docker's installer asks how to install, keep the recommended Per-user installation with WSL 2: CashPilot's checklist expects the WSL 2 backend. Leave Allow Windows Containers off: the apps run as Linux containers.
dockersteps.dockerInstall.running: Docker Desktop is installing in winget's window. Finish there; CashPilot waits
dockersteps.dockerUsers.title: Add your account to docker-users?
dockersteps.dockerUsers.heading: Add your account to docker-users
dockersteps.dockerUsers.changes: Windows adds your account, and only yours, to the docker-users group, so Docker Desktop lets you use it. CashPilot names your account by its ID (SID), read before the permission prompt, so it is your account that joins even when an administrator types their password.
dockersteps.dockerUsers.after: Windows applies a new group only after you sign out and back in; a restart works too. CashPilot asks you first: nothing signs you out until you click.
dockersteps.dockerUsers.undo: To undo, an administrator opens Computer Management, Local Users and Groups, Groups, docker-users, and removes your account.
dockersteps.dockerUsers.running: Windows is adding your account to docker-users
dockersteps.linuxEngine.title: Switch Docker to Linux containers?
dockersteps.linuxEngine.heading: Switch Docker to Linux containers
dockersteps.linuxEngine.changes: Docker Desktop switches from Windows containers to Linux containers. This changes all your Docker work, not only CashPilot's: Windows containers you run stop, and their images stay but do not show until you switch back.
dockersteps.linuxEngine.prompt: No Windows permission prompt: this is your own Docker Desktop setting.
dockersteps.linuxEngine.after: No restart. Docker's engine restarts, which takes a minute or two.
dockersteps.linuxEngine.undo: To switch back, right-click the Docker icon next to the clock and choose Switch to Windows containers.
dockersteps.linuxEngine.running: Docker Desktop is switching to Linux containers
dockersteps.hypervisorLaunch.title: Turn Windows' hypervisor back on?
dockersteps.hypervisorLaunch.heading: Turn Windows' hypervisor back on
dockersteps.hypervisorLaunch.changes: CashPilot first tries to read Windows' boot option hypervisorlaunchtype. If the read works and it is already auto, nothing changes and no restart follows. Otherwise Windows sets it to auto (with bcdedit), so its hypervisor starts at boot, as WSL 2 and Docker need. Older VirtualBox, VMware or Android emulator versions may have turned it off. Once it is on, they run on top of it and may be slower, and very old versions may not start their machines: update them to their newest versions.
dockersteps.hypervisorLaunch.after: A restart is needed only if CashPilot changed the boot option. Then CashPilot asks you first: nothing restarts until you click Restart now. If the read showed it was already auto, no restart follows.
dockersteps.hypervisorLaunch.undo: To undo, open PowerShell as administrator, run {command}, and restart. WSL 2 and Docker then stop working again.
dockersteps.hypervisorLaunch.running: Windows is turning its hypervisor back on
dockersteps.lanmanserverAuto.title: Set the Server service to Automatic?
dockersteps.lanmanserverAuto.heading: Set the Server service to Automatic
dockersteps.lanmanserverAuto.changes: Windows sets its Server service (LanmanServer) to start automatically, and starts it now. Docker Desktop needs it. The same service shares this PC's files and printers with your network, if you turned sharing on.
dockersteps.lanmanserverAuto.undo: To undo, open Services, find Server, and set its Startup type back to Manual or Disabled.
dockersteps.lanmanserverAuto.running: Windows is setting the Server service to Automatic

session.disclosure.title: Run {name} in your own session on this computer?
session.disclosure.intro: Earning apps sell your internet connection to other people. Their code is closed, and most of them ask for admin rights. They also update themselves. In your own session, nothing stands between these apps and your computer. If an app is hostile, or a bad update reaches it, the app can:
session.disclosure.risk.network: reach every device on your home network, such as your router's settings page, a NAS, cameras, printers and other computers.
session.disclosure.risk.vpn: reach your Tailscale, VPN or work network.
session.disclosure.risk.files: read your files, your browsers and the passwords that your browsers save.
session.disclosure.risk.logins: read the logins that CashPilot keeps for your earning accounts, and connect to CashPilot itself.
session.disclosure.risk.software: install other software, because most of these apps run as administrator.
session.disclosure.secureVM: The app can also change the protection of your Secure VM. When you set up the Secure VM, your Windows account got full control of Hyper-V. Apps in this session run as you. CashPilot detects the change and disconnects the VM within one minute.
session.disclosure.antivirus: Do not turn off antivirus scanning for the folder of an app. Some apps ask you to do this.
session.disclosure.traffic: Wherever an earning app runs, other people's traffic leaves through your internet address. Your internet provider may forbid this. If a buyer uses your connection for abuse, the abuse is traced to your address.

backups.title: Back these up
backups.intro: These services keep a node identity, a keystore or a wallet on this disk, and nothing else holds a copy. CashPilot refuses to delete these volumes, but it cannot protect them from a wiped disk, a new machine or {command}. Keep a copy somewhere else, then mark it as backed up. CashPilot asks again when the volume changes, and after six months.

server_commands.title: {server} can start and stop services on this computer
server_commands.help: It can deploy, stop, start, restart and remove the services of this computer's catalog, with the images CashPilot pins here. It cannot delete data that cannot be recovered, and it cannot change anything else on this computer.
server_commands.switch: Let {server} start and stop services on this computer
server_commands_wire.waiting: Waiting for the Windows administrator prompt...
server_commands_wire.allowed: Windows Firewall now lets your CashPilot reach this computer.
fleet.title: Across your CashPilot account
fleet.window: What the platforms this machine runs earned on your account over the last {days} days, reported by {server}{age}.
fleet.shared: {n} of these run on more than one machine, so the figure is the account's, not this machine's.
fleet.sharedTitle: More than one machine on your fleet runs this, so the provider reports one balance for all of them.
fleet.noFigures: This server has no figures for the platforms on this machine yet.
fleet.noReading: No reading at all for {slugs} — usually a collector that does not exist yet, or credentials never entered. They are missing from the total rather than counted as zero.
chart.empty.title: No earnings in the last {days} days
chart.empty.body: Daily earnings in {currency} appear here once a collected balance grows.
fleet_reach.reason.notListening: The fleet API is not running on this PC. Its port may be in use by another program.
fleet_reach.reason.thisPcOnly: The fleet API listens on {listen}, which only this PC can reach.
fleet_reach.reason.hubOff: Accept workers (hub mode) is off, so this PC turns away workers and phones that report to it.
fleet_reach.restartPending: You changed the fleet bind address or port in Settings. That takes effect after you restart CashPilot.
fleet_reach.open: Point CashPilot workers, mobile companions, or another machine on your LAN or tailnet at this desktop API. It listens on {listen}, takes authenticated heartbeats and registers devices automatically.
fleet_reach.steps.bind: set Fleet Bind Address to this PC's LAN or Tailscale address (or a free Fleet API Port if the port is in use)
fleet_reach.steps.both: set Accept workers (hub mode) to true, then set Fleet Bind Address to this PC's LAN or Tailscale address (or a free Fleet API Port if the port is in use)
fleet_reach.closed.title: Other machines cannot connect to this PC now.
fleet_reach.closed.body: A worker or phone set up to report here would not get through, so no setup snippet is shown.
fleet_reach.closed.howTo: To let them in: in Settings, {steps}, and restart CashPilot. Do this only on a home network or a tailnet you trust: any device that reaches this PC on that address can try the fleet API, and with metrics on it reads your earnings totals without a key. Most people do not need this: point workers and phones at a CashPilot server instead.
workercopies.unmanaged: Found by its image: CashPilot did not deploy it, so it takes no commands here.
workercopies.removeCopy: Remove copy {n} of {slug} from {worker}? This will stop and delete the container. Its data is kept.
workercopies.removeWithCopies: Remove {slug} from {worker}? This will stop and delete the container. {others, plural, one {Its other copy goes too.} other {Its # other copies go too.}} Its data is kept for a later deploy.
workercopies.removeService: Remove {slug} from {worker}? This will stop and delete the container. Its data is kept for a later deploy.
rating.title: Rating
fence_status.unknown: Docker status is unknown. CashPilot could not confirm the LAN fence.
fence_status.outside: {n, plural, one {# running earner is} other {# running earners are}} still outside it and can reach your LAN until redeployed.
fence_status.on.failed: Down: the fence could not be applied, so container deploys are refused. Needs attention says why.
fence_status.notChecked: Not checked yet. CashPilot checks it at start, before each deploy and every five minutes.
fence_status.on.empty: In place. No earner runs yet, so nothing is behind it.
fence_status.on.inPlace: In place: {n, plural, one {# running earner} other {# running earners}} behind it.
fence_status.legacy.outside: Not in place: {n, plural, one {# running earner can reach your LAN. Turn on isolation on the dashboard to fence it.} other {# running earners can reach your LAN. Turn on isolation on the dashboard to fence them.}}
fence_status.legacy.none: Not in place: this install deploys earners on Docker's default network, where they can reach your LAN. Set LAN isolation to on to fence the next deploy.
fence_status.off: Off: container earners use Docker's default network and can reach your LAN.
fence_status.unsupported: Not fenced: CashPilot cannot fence earners on this container runtime (Podman).
fence_status.failed: Not known: CashPilot could not check it. Needs attention says why.
fence_status.noEarner: No container earner runs now: {reason}. The fence is set up when Docker runs, at the latest on the first deploy.
stall_server.label: Almost no traffic
stall_server.note: Almost no traffic: your CashPilot at {url} compares the copies on this computer with the rest of your fleet, and shows those alerts. This computer still checks its proxied copies itself.
fleet_snippets.hidden: The key is hidden here. Copy puts the real key in your clipboard.
